metadata.case_name: CHAN WING v. CHAN WAI HUNG T/A HOLLY ENGINEERING CO

injuries.description: head injury with ASDH, cerebral contusion and skull fracture
source: CT brain showed right acute subdural haemorrhage (ASDH), cerebral contusion and skull fracture.
The neurosurgical diagnosis was head injury with ASDH, cerebral contusion and skull fracture.

injuries.description: left sided hemiparesis with total paralysis of left upper limb
source: He gradually recovered to GCS 15/15 and remained left side hemiparesis.
This amounts to a complete paralysis of his left arm and hand and what is now a mild weakness of his left leg.
(4) Left upper limb: This has remained totally paralysed but sensation is intact.
At his last follow up at the neurosurgical outpatient clinic on 2 February 2011, his left limb power was about grade 1/5 to 2/5.

(5) Left lower limb: His left leg has improved to the point that he can walk using a quadripod device, although he still sometimes scuffs his left foot and he has tripped a few times going to the bathroom at home.
Shortly after going home, the plaintiff suffered his first epileptic fit.
Between February 2011 and May 2012, he had frequent generalised convulsions that showed no particular pattern, except that they never occurred during sleep;
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: kept complaining of a severe headache
complete paralysis of his left arm and hand
mild weakness of his left leg
generalised convulsions (epileptic seizures) occurring approximately twice per month before medication
His speech is also slightly slurred
remains dependant on his family for dressing, baths, shopping and cooking
He walks slowly with a quadripod walking stick and cannot climb steps without help; he cannot go out on his own

treatments_received: Craniotomy for clot evacuation on 14 October 2010
Physiotherapy treatments at Shatin Hospital (Geriatric Day Hospital) and the neurological out-patient clinic of PMH

losses.description: remains dependant on his family for dressing, baths, shopping and cooking
He walks slowly with a quadripod walking stick and cannot climb steps without help; he cannot go out on his own

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: He never goes out on his own
Dr Choa considered he would not be fit to do work of any kind. His loss of earning capacity is 100%.
his life expectancy is reduced by 27% by reason of his injuries
